newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Device sees lower Q2 profits.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Device sees lower Q2 profits.

text.p: Integrated Device Technology Inc said on Thursday that revenues and earnings are expected to be lower than anticipated for its second quarter.
IDT said that revenue, for the quarter ending September 29, is expected to be more than 10 percent lower than in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
"A hoped for increase in bookings, especially turns bookings, did not occur in late August or September," said Len Perham, IDT's president and chief executive officer in a statement.

"Therefore we will not be able to achieve our earlier expectations for the quarter. The revenue shortfall, coupled with the start-up costs associated with our new Oregon manufacturing facility is causing us to lose money," he added.
The company said it is working on a wide ranging cost reduction plan that will be implemented before the end of the calendar year.
"Prices continued to decline in the standard static random access memory market and we expect this to remain the case into 1997," said Perham.
The company said it working to reduce manufacturing costs as low as possible adding that its other product areas were experiencing normal predictable pricing and ordering patterns.
Integrated is a maker of integrated circuits for a range of products inluding desktop computers.
Shares of the company closed 1/8 higher at 10-7/8 on Nasdaq.
